definitions.gloss: old-growth forest; mature forest; overmature stand
definitions.explanation: A forest that has reached an advanced stage of growth, typically consisting of large, old trees that have not been recently logged or significantly disturbed. Used in forestry as a technical classification of forest age.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{老齢林|ろうれいりん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{残|のこ}っている→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
examples.english: Old-growth forest remains on this mountain.

examples.japanese: {老齢林|ろうれいりん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{生物|せいぶつ}{多様性|たようせい}→生物多様性：04639_seibutsutayousei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{宝庫|ほうこ}→宝庫：17392_houko⟧だ。
examples.english: Old-growth forests are treasure troves of biodiversity.

examples.japanese: ⟦{伐採|ばっさい}→伐採：08435_bassai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{進|すす}み→進む：01225_susumu⟧、{老齢林|ろうれいりん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{面積|めんせき}→面積：05330_menseki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{年々|ねんねん}→年々：10417_nennen⟧⟦{減少|げんしょう}している→減少する：19026_genshousuru⟧。
examples.english: With continued logging, the area of old-growth forest is decreasing year by year.

notes:
A forestry term composed of ⟦{老齢|ろうれい}→老齢：29085_rourei⟧ (old age, advanced age) and {林|りん} (forest, grove). In Japanese forestry, forests are classified by age: {幼齢林|ようれいりん} (young forest), {壮齢林|そうれいりん} (mature forest), and {老齢林|ろうれいりん} (old-growth forest).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {老齢林|ろうれいりん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{保護|ほご}→保護：03625_hogo⟧: protection of old-growth forests
- {老齢林|ろうれいりん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{伐採|ばっさい}→伐採：08435_bassai⟧: logging of old-growth forests
- ⟦{天然|てんねん}→天然：03560_tennen⟧{老齢林|ろうれいりん}: natural old-growth forest

FOREST AGE CLASSIFICATION:
- {幼齢林|ようれいりん}: young forest (roughly 1-20 years)
- {壮齢林|そうれいりん}: middle-aged forest
- {老齢林|ろうれいりん}: old-growth forest (species-dependent, typically 80+ years)
